descriptors.definition: An intangible asset acquired in a business combination must be recognized separately from goodwill if it satisfies either the contractual-legal criterion or the separability criterion. These assets are identifiable even when they are not transferable or separable from the acquiree.
inclusion: Licences to operate power plants
Technology patents
Assets capable of being separated, sold, licensed, or exchanged
exclusion: Unidentifiable future economic benefits grouped inside unallocated goodwill
nearby_distinctions: Contractual-legal items do not require transferability, whereas separability requires the asset to be capable of individual exchange.

descriptors.definition: A reacquired right is an identifiable intangible asset recognized when an acquirer reacquires a right previously granted to the acquiree to use specific assets. Any difference between contract terms and current market transactions is recognized as a settlement gain or loss.
inclusion: Rights to use the acquirer's trade name
Rights to use the acquirer's technology under licensing agreements
exclusion: Newly originated rights created directly between the combined parties post-combination
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard acquired intangibles because they originate from a prior contract between the acquirer and acquiree.

descriptors.definition: Goodwill is recognized at the acquisition date as the excess of the aggregate consideration transferred, non-controlling interest, and previously held equity interests over the net identifiable assets acquired. In rare situations where net assets exceed consideration, a bargain purchase gain is recognized.
inclusion: Purchase consideration fair value
Non-controlling interest proportional or fair value measurements
exclusion: Transaction costs associated with the business combination
nearby_distinctions: Positive excess results in goodwill assets, whereas excess of net assets over consideration results in bargain purchase capital reserves.

descriptors.definition: A bargain purchase occurs when the net identifiable assets acquired exceed the total purchase consideration. The resulting gain is recognized in equity as a capital reserve after the acquirer reassesses the identification and measurement of all acquired items.
inclusion: Gains from regulatory requirement sales
Gains from bankruptcy or distressed sales
exclusion: Standard acquisitions where purchase consideration exceeds or equals net asset values
nearby_distinctions: Unlike standard goodwill generation, bargain purchases yield negative goodwill balances credited directly to capital reserves.

descriptors.definition: The measurement period is a defined window up to one year following the acquisition date allowing provisional amounts to be retrospectively adjusted for new information. Changes reflecting conditions existing at the acquisition date adjust goodwill, while subsequent changes are treated as errors.
inclusion: Adjustments for facts existing at the acquisition date
New asset and liability recognitions discovered during the window
exclusion: Adjustments driven by events occurring after the acquisition date
nearby_distinctions: Limited strictly to a maximum of one year, after which valuation corrections must follow standard error-correction rules.

descriptors.concept_name: Determining what is part of the Business Combination Transaction
descriptors.definition: Acquirers must isolate and exclude transactions that are separate from the exchange for the acquiree. Separate transactions are those arranged primarily for the benefit of the acquirer rather than the acquiree prior to combination.
inclusion: Settlements of pre-existing relationships
Remuneration for post-combination employee services
exclusion: Core consideration directly exchanged for the equity interests or assets of the acquiree
nearby_distinctions: Differs from consideration transferred by serving acquirer-centric objectives rather than compensating former owners for the business.

descriptors.concept_name: Contingent Payments to Employees or Selling Shareholders
descriptors.definition: Contingent payments to selling shareholders who become employees are evaluated to determine whether they represent contingent consideration or remuneration for post-combination services. Factors such as employment forfeiture clauses and employment duration help clarify the substance of the payments.
inclusion: Payments automatically forfeited upon termination of employment
Contingent arrangements tied to required employment periods
exclusion: Unconditional purchase consideration distributed uniformly to all former owners
nearby_distinctions: Classified as post-combination employee expense if dependent on continued employment, rather than part of the purchase price.

descriptors.concept_name: Acquirer Share Based Payment Awards Exchanged for Awards held by the Acquiree’s Employees
descriptors.definition: Exchanges of share-based payment awards in a business combination are accounted for as award modifications. The portion of the replacement award attributable to pre-combination service is included in measuring consideration transferred, while unearned portions are treated as post-combination remuneration.
inclusion: Replacement awards mandated by acquisition agreement terms
Market-based measures remeasured on the acquisition date
exclusion: Awards replaced voluntarily by the acquirer when not legally or contractually obliged to do so
nearby_distinctions: Mandatory replacements split value between consideration and remuneration, whereas voluntary replacements for expired awards are fully expensed.

descriptors.definition: When an acquirer does not exchange outstanding share-based payment awards of the acquiree, they are measured at their market-based measure. Vested awards and the pre-combination portion of unvested awards form part of the non-controlling interest.
inclusion: Vested share awards classified within non-controlling interest
Pre-combination portions of unvested acquiree awards
exclusion: Replacement awards issued directly by the acquirer
nearby_distinctions: Unvested non-replacement portions split across non-controlling interest for pre-combination service and employee cost for post-combination service.

descriptors.definition: Non-controlling interest components representing present ownership entitlements can be measured either at fair value or at the proportionate share of identifiable net assets. Valuation differences between the acquirer and non-controlling interests often reflect control premiums or ownership discounts.
inclusion: Present ownership interests entitling holders to proportionate net asset shares
Quoted market price valuations
exclusion: Controlling equity interests held directly by the parent acquirer
nearby_distinctions: Acquirer per-share values typically incorporate control premiums, whereas non-controlling interests may factor in discounts for lack of control.

descriptors.definition: Assets and liabilities acquired in a business combination are subsequently accounted for under applicable standards, with specific guidance provided for items like reacquired rights, contingent liabilities, and indemnification assets. Reacquired rights are amortized over remaining contractual terms.
inclusion: Amortization of reacquired rights over remaining contract periods
Subsequent measurement of contingent liabilities at higher of Ind AS 37 and initial amounts
exclusion: Initial purchase price allocation adjustments occurring inside the measurement period
nearby_distinctions: Governs post-acquisition tracking and rule applications distinct from initial acquisition-date fair value determinations.

descriptors.definition: Contingent consideration fair value changes reflecting pre-acquisition facts and circumstances are treated as measurement period adjustments impacting goodwill. Changes arising from post-acquisition events are recognized in profit or loss or equity according to applicable standards.
inclusion: Fair value updates based on pre-acquisition conditions
Adjustments impacting goodwill during the measurement window
exclusion: Changes driven by post-acquisition milestones, earnings targets, or share price achievements
nearby_distinctions: Pre-existing condition adjustments modify goodwill, whereas post-combination milestone achievements bypass goodwill and route through earnings or equity.
